- Start sessions with the project work, not doctor/stack checks. Run `claude-stack-doctor` only after a second failure.
- Let small breakage (noisy logs, stale counts, duplicate hooks) wait if there is a workaround.

**Why:** A 60-day measurement to 2026-10-03 estimated ~55% system / 45% real work (commits: 65/35). Eric wants more time creating and shipping. He chose to handle system work as it comes up instead of in a fixed slot.

**How to apply:** Do system work when it is needed, without a time box. Still start with project work. Do not propose new system pieces unasked. A ratio recheck is on the calendar for 2026-11-02 (method in the event notes); the goal is real work above 50%.

Related: [[working-conditions-bottleneck]], [[skill-bloat-and-promotion]], [[session-hygiene]].
---
name: working-conditions-bottleneck
description: "Eric's self-identified bottleneck is working conditions, not effort — he needs a thinking partner / sharing outlet, and lacking one he goes looking for people and loses time"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: user
  originSessionId: 583baf57-8dc4-46c7-8842-501ae1fdeb04
  modified: 2026-08-03T23:18:09.932Z
---

Eric's limiting factor on deep work is environmental, not motivational. He is highly productive in short bursts once work actually starts; what breaks is the path to starting. The specific disruptor he named (2026-07-28) is the pull to share what he's working on — with no standing outlet for it, he goes and finds people, which costs him the session.

**Corrected 2026-07-29.** The pull toward people is not a leak, it's the generative stage. His own observation: alone he wants company; in company the project ideas arrive. Solitude is where he refines, not where he generates. A long unbroken solo block with nothing in the hopper is waiting, not deep work.

**Second brake, same day:** he holds ideas back from fear of overstepping into others' lanes, against an unstated expectation that he act unasked. He is deliberately moving off this position ("if I don't act, ideas wither"). Pressfield's Resistance is his frame for it.

**Qualified 2026-08-03.** The permission gate is not entirely self-imposed. He acted unasked on a device another staffer was already championing (ShiftWave chair, second trial unit) and took real organizational blowback for it — careful, low-key handling bought nothing, because the claim was made by initiating, not by presenting. So the caution is warranted on ground someone has visibly attached themselves to, and unwarranted everywhere else. His same-day reaction ("pander to the people in power, keep your head down") is a bruise, not necessarily a settled position — don't treat it as one.

**Why:** Both reframe what looks like procrastination. The first is an unmet structural need (input/ideation) improvising in real time; the second is a self-imposed permission gate that reads as professional courtesy. Neither is a discipline failure, and treating them as one produces useless advice.

**How to apply:** Act as the thinking partner in-session — reflect his reasoning back, name what's interesting in it, and give him something to react to rather than only executing tasks silently. When he's ideating, don't rush to implementation; the ideation *is* the need being met, and it's the stage that feeds everything else — help him capture what surfaces. Prefer short, well-scoped blocks with a clear starting line. When he hesitates on whether something is his to do, first ask whether anyone has visibly claimed it — if not, name the permission gate rather than validating the caution; if someone has, the hesitation is a correct read and the useful move is how to approach the owner, not encouragement to proceed. Related: [[company-generates-solitude-refines]], [[waiting-for-the-ask-kills-the-idea]], [[ownership-not-merit-governs-the-reaction]], [[design-the-conditions-not-the-discipline]] in the SecondBrain vault.

Solitude is where he refines, not where he generates. A long unbroken solo block with nothing in the hopper is waiting, not deep work.

**Second brake, same day:** he holds ideas back from fear of overstepping into others' lanes, against an unstated expectation that he act unasked. He is deliberately moving off this position ("if I don't act, ideas wither"). Pressfield's Resistance is his frame for it.

**Qualified 2026-08-03.** The permission gate is not entirely self-imposed. He acted unasked on a device another staffer was already championing (ShiftWave chair, second trial unit) and took real organizational blowback for it — careful, low-key handling bought nothing, because the claim was made by initiating, not by presenting. So the caution is warranted on ground someone has visibly attached themselves to, and unwarranted everywhere else. His same-day reaction ("pander to the people in power, keep your head down") is a bruise, not necessarily a settled position — don't treat it as one.

The first is an unmet structural need (input/ideation) improvising in real time; the second is a self-imposed permission gate that reads as professional courtesy. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy all of ~/DEV to the Google Drive _MACHINE/Cloud_Copy folder (one-way, never deletes).

Runs daily from launchd (com.keystone.clouddrivepush, 07:00 and 17:30) and can be run by hand.
Builds the file list fresh each run, so new and changed files are picked up.

Approved scope (Eric, 2026-10-12): all project files, including athlete data, on personal Google Drive.
Kept local on purpose:
  - database files (DuckDB/SQLite): sync can lock or corrupt them.
    daily-backup.ps1 uploads consistent copies as dev-databases.tgz via gws instead.
  - password and key files (.env, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa, credentials*, secrets*)
  - regenerable folders (node_modules, .venv, venv, __pycache__, .next)
  - any folder whose CLAUDE.md heading says "local only" (STORAGE.md rule; e.g. SpecialRequests/TOS_ES)
  - browser profiles (a folder holding "Local State"): saved logins and cookies
Log: ~/.claude/scripts/logs/cloud-push.log. Failures also go to global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log,
so they show at the next session start.
"""
import datetime
import os
import subprocess
import sys

DEV = os.path.expanduser("~/DEV")
DEST = os.path.expanduser(
    "~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV")  # moved out of Primary 2026-10-14
LOG = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/scripts/logs/cloud-push.log")
LIST = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/scripts/logs/cloud-push-files0.bin")
DB_EXT = (".duckdb", ".db", ".sqlite", ".sqlite3", ".db-wal", ".db-shm")
SECRET_PREFIX = (".env",)
SECRET_PARTS = ("credentials", "secrets", "id_rsa", ".pem", ".key")
REGEN_DIRS = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", ".next", ".build", "printing-press-library"}
JUNK = {".DS_Store"}
ERRORS = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log")


def log(msg):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(LOG), exist_ok=True)
    line = f"{datetime.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')} {msg}"
    with open(LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(line + "\n")
    print(line)
    if msg.startswith("ERROR"):
        stamp = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
        with open(ERRORS, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(f"[{stamp}] cloud-push: {msg[:300]}\n")


def private_dir(dp, fn):
    """True for a folder that must not leave this Mac: local-only CLAUDE.md, or a browser profile."""
    if "Local State" in fn:
        return True
    if "CLAUDE.md" in fn:
        with open(os.path.join(dp, "CLAUDE.md"), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            return "local only" in fh.readline().lower()
    return False


def keep(name):
    low = name.lower()
    if low in JUNK:
        return False
    if low.endswith(DB_EXT):
        return False
    if low.startswith(SECRET_PREFIX) or any(p in low for p in SECRET_PARTS):
        return False
    return True


def build_list():
    files = []
    for dp, dn, fn in os.walk(DEV):
        if private_dir(dp, fn):
            dn[:] = []
            continue
        base = os.path.basename(dp)
        dn[:] = [
            d for d in dn
            if d not in REGEN_DIRS and not (base == "graphify-out" and d == "cache")
        ]
        for f in fn:
            if not keep(f):
                continue
            p = os.path.join(dp, f)
            if os.path.islink(p) or not os.path.isfile(p):
                continue
            files.append(os.path.relpath(p, DEV))
    return files


def main():
    if not os.path.isdir(DEST.rsplit("/Cloud_Copy", 1)[0]):
        log("ERROR Drive not mounted; nothing copied")
        return 1
    os.makedirs(DEST, exist_ok=True)
    files = build_list()
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(LIST), exist_ok=True)
    with open(LIST, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(b"\0".join(f.encode("utf-8") for f in files) + b"\0")
    log(f"START {len(files)} files listed")
    # No --delete flag: rsync never removes files on the Drive side, so this stays one-way.
    cmd = ["/usr/bin/rsync", "-a", "--modify-window=5", "--from0",
           f"--files-from={LIST}", DEV + "/", DEST + "/"]
    res = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if res.returncode != 0:
        log(f"ERROR rsync exit {res.returncode}: {res.stderr.strip()[-300:]}")
        return res.returncode
    log(f"OK rsync finished ({len(files)} files checked; only changed files were copied)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
----
"""Checks cloud-push.py's file list keeps private folders off the Drive mirror.
Run: python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/test_cloud_push.py  (builds a temp tree; copies nothing)
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import tempfile

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "cloud_push", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "cloud-push.py"))
cp = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(cp)


def touch(root, rel, text="x"):
    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
    with open(p, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(text)


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as dev:
    touch(dev, "CLAUDE.md", "# ~/DEV — map\nA folder whose CLAUDE.md says local only stays local.\n")
    touch(dev, "Proj/notes.md")
    touch(dev, "Proj/.env")
    touch(dev, "Private/CLAUDE.md", "# Private — local only\n")
    touch(dev, "Private/case.csv")
    touch(dev, "Proj/out/edge-profile/Local State")
    touch(dev, "Proj/out/edge-profile/Default/Login Data")
    cp.DEV = dev
    got = set(cp.build_list())
    assert got == {"CLAUDE.md", "Proj/notes.md"}, got
print("ok")

Anything rsyncing into the Google Drive for Desktop mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*/`) needs `--modify-window=5`. Drive stores an mtime 1–2s below what rsync set, and for large files it stamps its own upload time instead (skew of hours). rsync's quick-check is size+mtime, so byte-identical files read as changed and are re-sent on **every** run, permanently.

Diagnosed 2026-08-14 on `daily-backup.ps1` → `codex/sessions`: all 256 files size-identical, yet 134 re-sent nightly (252 MB). That perpetual write load into FUSE is what fed the wedge the watchdog was catching — the snapshot had been failing since 2026-08-06 (rsync exit 23, then 1, then 124 once the watchdog landed).

**Why:** `du` on the mount reports less than the source (171M vs 289M) because Drive doesn't materialize every file — that discrepancy looks like an incomplete mirror and sends you hunting for missing data that isn't missing. Compare `stat -f%z` per file, not `du`.

**How to apply:**
- Diagnose with dry runs, not `du`: `rsync -an -i <src>/ <dst>/ | grep -c '^>f'` with and without `--modify-window=5`. A large gap between the two *is* the diagnosis.
- Files already stamped with Drive's own upload time need a one-time `touch -r <src> <dst>`; the flag alone won't close a multi-hour skew. The repair sticks across Drive re-sync.
- Never substitute `--size-only` — `claude-projects` has genuine same-size edits that only mtime catches.
- Genuinely-new files re-send under both settings (gemini's 428 were all NEW). If the count is identical with and without the window, it's real work, not this bug.

**`--modify-window` has a blind spot — cover it for SQLite (found 2026-08-15 while reviewing the fix).** The window makes rsync's quick-check tolerate a 5s mtime difference. That is safe for append-only logs, where any real change also moves the size. It is NOT safe for files rewritten in place at identical size — SQLite updates rows inside existing pages, so `~/.codex/sqlite/codex-dev.db` (229,376 B) can change content with size unchanged. If that write lands within 5s of the dest's Drive-rounded mtime, rsync skips it, and keeps skipping forever because neither side changes again.

Reproduced: two 8-byte files, same size, content differing, mtimes 3s apart → `--modify-window=5` copies **0** files (silent loss); adding `--checksum` copies **1**. Fix in `daily-backup.ps1`: `Invoke-Rsync`/`Snapshot` take an `$extraArgs` param and the `.codex/sqlite` snapshot alone passes `--checksum`. Do not apply `--checksum` broadly — it re-reads every byte on both sides; it is cheap only because that DB is ~224 KB.

**How to apply:** when adding a new `Snapshot` call, ask whether the source can change without changing size. Databases, fixed-width records, and image/binary formats with in-place headers all can — give those `--checksum`. Logs and transcripts cannot — leave them on the window.

**One-way copy of new files into Drive: use `--ignore-existing`, never `--update` (2026-10-02).** `rsync -a --update` from `~/DEV/S2_Evaluation/data/` into the Drive mount hung 11 min, with nothing copied. `--update` did not skip files already on Drive, because Drive's mtimes are its own. The receiving child was blocked reading an existing Drive file. `--ignore-existing` copied the 2 missing files at once. macOS rsync is openrsync: its receiving child shows as `rsync --server`, so `pgrep -f "rsync -a ..."` misses it. Stop a hung run with TaskStop, not `kill`.

name: drive-fuse-rsync-mtime-loop
description: "Google Drive CloudStorage rounds mtimes it didn't write, making rsync -a re-send byte-identical files forever; fix is --modify-window=5"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa062f93-2c55-4016-b9c6-f1a32e0a7083
  modified: 2026-10-02T21:48:00.682Z
---

Anything rsyncing into the Google Drive for Desktop mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*/`) needs `--modify-window=5`. Drive stores an mtime 1–2s below what rsync set, and for large files it stamps its own upload time instead (skew of hours). rsync's quick-check is size+mtime, so byte-identical files read as changed and are re-sent on **every** run, permanently.

Diagnosed 2026-08-14 on `daily-backup.ps1` → `codex/sessions`: all 256 files size-identical, yet 134 re-sent nightly (252 MB). That perpetual write load into FUSE is what fed the wedge the watchdog was catching — the snapshot had been failing since 2026-08-06 (rsync exit 23, then 1, then 124 once the watchdog landed).

**Why:** `du` on the mount reports less than the source (171M vs 289M) because Drive doesn't materialize every file — that discrepancy looks like an incomplete mirror and sends you hunting for missing data that isn't missing. Compare `stat -f%z` per file, not `du`.

**How to apply:**
- Diagnose with dry runs, not `du`: `rsync -an -i <src>/ <dst>/ | grep -c '^>f'` with and without `--modify-window=5`. A large gap between the two *is* the diagnosis.
- Files already stamped with Drive's own upload time need a one-time `touch -r <src> <dst>`; the flag alone won't close a multi-hour skew. The repair sticks across Drive re-sync.
- Never substitute `--size-only` — `claude-projects` has genuine same-size edits that only mtime catches.
- Genuinely-new files re-send under both settings (gemini's 428 were all NEW). If the count is identical with and without the window, it's real work, not this bug.

**`--modify-window` has a blind spot — cover it for SQLite (found 2026-08-15 while reviewing the fix).** The window makes rsync's quick-check tolerate a 5s mtime difference. That is safe for append-only logs, where any real change also moves the size. It is NOT safe for files rewritten in place at identical size — SQLite updates rows inside existing pages, so `~/.codex/sqlite/codex-dev.db` (229,376 B) can change content with size unchanged. If that write lands within 5s of the dest's Drive-rounded mtime, rsync skips it, and keeps skipping forever because neither side changes again.

Reproduced: two 8-byte files, same size, content differing, mtimes 3s apart → `--modify-window=5` copies **0** files (silent loss); adding `--checksum` copies **1**. Fix in `daily-backup.ps1`: `Invoke-Rsync`/`Snapshot` take an `$extraArgs` param and the `.codex/sqlite` snapshot alone passes `--checksum`. Do not apply `--checksum` broadly — it re-reads every byte on both sides; it is cheap only because that DB is ~224 KB.

**How to apply:** when adding a new `Snapshot` call, ask whether the source can change without changing size. Databases, fixed-width records, and image/binary formats with in-place headers all can — give those `--checksum`. Logs and transcripts cannot — leave them on the window.

**One-way copy of new files into Drive: use `--ignore-existing`, never `--update` (2026-10-02).** `rsync -a --update` from `~/DEV/S2_Evaluation/data/` into the Drive mount hung 11 min, with nothing copied. `--update` did not skip files already on Drive, because Drive's mtimes are its own. The receiving child was blocked reading an existing Drive file. `--ignore-existing` copied the 2 missing files at once. macOS rsync is openrsync: its receiving child shows as `rsync --server`, so `pgrep -f "rsync -a ..."` misses it. Stop a hung run with TaskStop, not `kill`.

#!/bin/bash
# Launcher for com.keystone.clouddrivepush (07:00, 17:30). launchd runs `open -g -a Terminal` on this
# file, so cloud-push.py runs with Terminal's Google Drive access.
# Why: run straight from launchd, macOS lets a job create new Drive files but blocks listing Drive

    >> "$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/cloud-push.out" 2>> "$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/cloud-push.err"
exit 0

#!/bin/bash
# launchd entry for com.keystone.clouddrivepush: opens cloud-push.command in Terminal (see that file for why),
# then checks that the copy started. Terminal may not open a window while the screen is locked; without this
# check a skipped run would leave no line anywhere.
LOG="$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/cloud-push.log"
ERRORS="$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log"
before=$(grep -c ' START ' "$LOG" 2>/dev/null)
/usr/bin/open -g -a Terminal "$HOME/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.command"
for _ in $(seq 1 18); do
    sleep 5
    [ "$(grep -c ' START ' "$LOG" 2>/dev/null)" -gt "$before" ] && exit 0
done
msg="ERROR cloud-push did not start within 90 s (Terminal did not open it; screen locked?)"
echo "$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S) $msg" >> "$LOG"
echo "[$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00)] cloud-push: $msg" >> "$ERRORS"
exit 1

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-` (Mac `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`; Windows `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV`; `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` → `00-Primary-Storage-Drive`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

name: cloud-push-launchd-blocked
description: "cloud-push under launchd: macOS per-file com.apple.macl blocks it; fixed 2026-10-23 by running it inside Terminal via cloud-push-launch.sh"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 802ea68a-c53e-4d3a-a897-1d311560fdd1
  modified: 2026-10-23T12:30:00.000Z
---

`com.keystone.clouddrivepush` (07:00 and 17:30) failed under launchd from 2026-10-12 to 10-23 with rsync `open: Operation not permitted` on `Drive/.../_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV/`. By hand from Terminal it always worked.

**Cause (tested 2026-10-23).** A process started straight by launchd (python3 or bash) can stat, mkdir and create new files in the Drive mount, and rewrite files it made itself. It cannot list Drive folders, or open, rename over, or delete files that Terminal made. Each such file carries `com.apple.macl` naming Terminal; `xattr -d` does not remove it. Full Disk Access on `Python.app`/rsync does not help (tried 10-14). rsync lists the destination, so it failed on the first step.

**Fix (live 2026-10-23).** The plist runs `/bin/bash ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push-launch.sh`. That runs `open -g -a Terminal ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.command`, which runs `cloud-push.py` (rsync, unchanged) with Terminal's access. The launcher waits 90 s for a new `START` line in `cloud-push.log`; if none, it writes an ERROR to the log and to `.errors.log`. Tracked plist copy: `~/.claude/scripts/com.keystone.clouddrivepush.plist`. Proven: kickstarted runs OK 07:15 and 07:21 with the screen locked.

**Known costs.** Each run leaves a Terminal window open (profile "Clear Dark" does not close on exit; an osascript self-close did not work). Under memory pressure Terminal ran queued opens ~5 min late; the 90 s check would log that as an ERROR even if the copy runs later.

**How to apply:** Do not swap rsync for a launchd-run copier: Terminal-made files can never be updated that way, and a by-hand run re-taints files. By hand is still `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py`, or `launchctl kickstart gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Off switch: `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Any other launchd job that must read or change Terminal-made Drive files hits the same wall; route it through Terminal the same way or use the `gws` API. See [[automation-cadence]] and [[cloud-copy-approval]].

metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 802ea68a-c53e-4d3a-a897-1d311560fdd1
  modified: 2026-10-23T12:30:00.000Z
---

`com.keystone.clouddrivepush` (07:00 and 17:30) failed under launchd from 2026-10-12 to 10-23 with rsync `open: Operation not permitted` on `Drive/.../_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV/`. By hand from Terminal it always worked.

**Cause (tested 2026-10-23).** A process started straight by launchd (python3 or bash) can stat, mkdir and create new files in the Drive mount, and rewrite files it made itself. It cannot list Drive folders, or open, rename over, or delete files that Terminal made. Each such file carries `com.apple.macl` naming Terminal; `xattr -d` does not remove it. Full Disk Access on `Python.app`/rsync does not help (tried 10-14). rsync lists the destination, so it failed on the first step.

**Fix (live 2026-10-23).** The plist runs `/bin/bash ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push-launch.sh`. That runs `open -g -a Terminal ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.command`, which runs `cloud-push.py` (rsync, unchanged) with Terminal's access. The launcher waits 90 s for a new `START` line in `cloud-push.log`; if none, it writes an ERROR to the log and to `.errors.log`. Tracked plist copy: `~/.claude/scripts/com.keystone.clouddrivepush.plist`. Proven: kickstarted runs OK 07:15 and 07:21 with the screen locked.

**Known costs.** Each run leaves a Terminal window open (profile "Clear Dark" does not close on exit; an osascript self-close did not work). Under memory pressure Terminal ran queued opens ~5 min late; the 90 s check would log that as an ERROR even if the copy runs later.

**How to apply:** Do not swap rsync for a launchd-run copier: Terminal-made files can never be updated that way, and a by-hand run re-taints files. By hand is still `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py`, or `launchctl kickstart gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Off switch: `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Any other launchd job that must read or change Terminal-made Drive files hits the same wall; route it through Terminal the same way or use the `gws` API. See [[automation-cadence]] and [[cloud-copy-approval]].

# daily-backup.ps1 — KeystoneOS durability automation (macOS port, 2026-08-05)
# Runs daily at 00:30 via launchd agent "com.keystone.dailybackup".
# Windows original preserved at daily-backup.ps1.win-orig.
#
# Jobs:
#   1. Git-sync the memory repos (auto-commit + push).
#   2. Snapshot non-git stores to the cloud targets (rsync, ADDITIVE - no delete).
#   3. Manifest-driven coverage. backup-manifest.json is the single authority.
#
# COVERAGE MODEL — three states, all covered (each gap was a real failure):
#   tracked + committed + pushed  -> GitHub
#   untracked or ignored          -> SSD (captureOrphans)
#   tracked + modified            -> SSD (captureWorkingTree)
# DEFAULT-DENY: a DEV directory absent from the manifest raises an error.
# Never reintroduce repo-detection as a coverage test.

param([switch]$DryRun)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$U = $HOME
# ~/DEV on the Mac, ~/Desktop/DEV on Windows. Resolved the same way as memsearch-sync.js
# (2026-09-30): the hardcoded "$U/DEV" made every Windows run fall back to the 5-path index
# list and report all 52 DEV dirs "absent from disk".
$DevRoot = @("$U/DEV", "$U/Desktop/DEV") | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath "$_/KeystoneOS" } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $DevRoot) { $DevRoot = "$U/DEV" }
$LogDir = "$U/.claude/scripts/logs"
$LogFile = "$LogDir/daily-backup.log"
$StateFile = "$LogDir/backup-state.json"
$ErrorsLog = "$U/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log"
$Errors = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
# Per-copy wall-clock ceiling for Invoke-Rsync's watchdog. Generous: the largest healthy
# snapshot here finishes in seconds, so anything near this is wedged, not busy.
$RsyncTimeoutSec = 900
$Results = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $LogDir | Out-Null

# daily-backup.ps1 — KeystoneOS durability automation (macOS port, 2026-08-05)
# Runs daily at 00:30 via launchd agent "com.keystone.dailybackup".
# Windows original preserved at daily-backup.ps1.win-orig.
#
# Jobs:
#   1. Git-sync the memory repos (auto-commit + push).
#   2. Snapshot non-git stores to the cloud targets (rsync, ADDITIVE - no delete).
#   3. Manifest-driven coverage. backup-manifest.json is the single authority.
#
# COVERAGE MODEL — three states, all covered (each gap was a real failure):
#   tracked + committed + pushed  -> GitHub
#   untracked or ignored          -> SSD (captureOrphans)
#   tracked + modified            -> SSD (captureWorkingTree)
# DEFAULT-DENY: a DEV directory absent from the manifest raises an error.
# Never reintroduce repo-detection as a coverage test.

param([switch]$DryRun)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$U = $HOME
# ~/DEV on the Mac, ~/Desktop/DEV on Windows. Resolved the same way as memsearch-sync.js
# (2026-09-30): the hardcoded "$U/DEV" made every Windows run fall back to the 5-path index
# list and report all 52 DEV dirs "absent from disk".
$DevRoot = @("$U/DEV", "$U/Desktop/DEV") | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath "$_/KeystoneOS" } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $DevRoot) { $DevRoot = "$U/DEV" }
$LogDir = "$U/.claude/scripts/logs"
$LogFile = "$LogDir/daily-backup.log"
$StateFile = "$LogDir/backup-state.json"
$ErrorsLog = "$U/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log"
$Errors = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
# Per-copy wall-clock ceiling for Invoke-Rsync's watchdog. Generous: the largest healthy
# snapshot here finishes in seconds, so anything near this is wedged, not busy.
$RsyncTimeoutSec = 900
$Results = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $LogDir | Out-Null

content.text: One fix: stamp the time from *before* the copy starts, so edits made during the upload are not missed.

cd ~/.claude/scripts && python3 - <<'EOF'
p = "daily-backup.ps1"; s = open(p).read()
a = "    $stage = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) \"zotero-$([guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))\"\n"
assert s.count(a) == 1
s = s.replace(a, "    $started = Get-Date  # stamp with the start time, so edits made during the upload count as changes next time\n" + a)
b = """            if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $stamp) { (Get-Item -LiteralPath $stamp).LastWriteTime = Get-Date }
            else { New-Item -ItemType File -Path $stamp | Out-Null }"""
assert s.count(b) == 1
s = s.replace(b, """            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $stamp)) { New-Item -ItemType File -Path $stamp | Out-Null }
            (Get-Item -LiteralPath $stamp).LastWriteTime = $started""")
open(p, "w").write(s)
EOF

# Harness: load only the functions Snapshot-Zotero needs from daily-backup.ps1, then run it.
param([string]$StampDir)
$path = "$HOME/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1"
$errs = $null
$ast = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($path, [ref]$null, [ref]$errs)
if ($errs) { $errs | ForEach-Object { "PARSE ERROR: $($_.Message)" }; exit 1 }
"parse ok"
$U = $HOME
$LogDir = $StampDir
$DryRun = $false
$Errors = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
$Results = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
function Log($msg) { "LOG $msg" | Out-Host }
$want = 'Invoke-GwsJson', 'Snapshot-Gws', 'Snapshot-Zotero'
$ast.FindAll({ $args[0] -is [System.Management.Automation.Language.FunctionDefinitionAst] -and $want -contains $args[0].Name }, $false) |
    ForEach-Object { . ([scriptblock]::Create($_.Extent.Text)) }
foreach ($a in $ast.EndBlock.Statements) {
    if ($a.Extent.Text -match '^\$(GwsExe|Drive\w+Id)\s*=|^if \(-not \$GwsExe\)') { . ([scriptblock]::Create($a.Extent.Text)) }
}
"gws=$GwsExe machine=$DriveMachineId"
"--- run 1 (no stamp: should upload)"
Snapshot-Zotero
"errors=$($Errors -join ',') stamp=$((Get-Item "$StampDir/zotero-snapshot.stamp" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).LastWriteTime)"
"--- run 2 (fresh stamp: should skip weekly)"
Snapshot-Zotero
"--- run 3 (stamp 8 days old, nothing newer: should skip unchanged)"
$st = Get-Item "$StampDir/zotero-snapshot.stamp"
$st.LastWriteTime = (Get-Date).AddDays(-8)
& /usr/bin/touch -t 202601010000 "$StampDir/fake"
# Pretend nothing changed: point the check at a stamp newer than every Zotero file but older than 7 days.
$st.LastWriteTime = [datetime]::Parse('2026-10-16 23:59')
Snapshot-Zotero

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# STORAGE — where every file lives

Read this before you save, move, back up, or copy any file. One rule set for every agent
(Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) on every machine. Decided by Eric 2026-10-16.

## The model

Every file has one **true copy**. Edit the true copy, or a working copy that syncs back to it
the same day. Everything else is a **backup** (machine-written, never edited) or **scratch**
(thrown away).

Drive is the one place Eric looks. Documents live there directly. Code lives in GitHub and is
mirrored into Drive, so Drive still shows everything.

## Where things go

| What you are saving | True copy | Work on it at | Gets back to the true copy by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document, PDF, deck, spreadsheet for humans | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`, filed by its `README.md` ladder | Drive desktop app, or `~/DEV/_DRIVE` | Drive sync (automatic) |
| Finished deliverable from a repo | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/03_REPORTS/`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>` | made in `<repo>/outputs/` | `closeout` copies it (copy, keep the repo one) |
| Code, scripts, project docs, `STATUS.md` | GitHub `erash11/<repo>` | `~/DEV/<repo>` | `git commit` + `git push`, every session |
| Generated output (charts, exports, logs) | `<repo>/outputs/` | same | regenerate from code; gitignore it if large |
| Database (DuckDB, SQLite) | local disk, inside its repo or `~/DEV` | same | nightly `daily-backup.ps1` stages the live DBs (not dated `before`/`backup` copies) into `dev-databases.tgz`, uploaded via `gws` to Drive `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` (since 2026-10-20; one copy, no history) |
| Secrets (`.env`, tokens, keys) | macOS Keychain or local `.env` | same | nowhere else — never in git, Drive, or chat |
| Claude/Codex config, skills, memory | GitHub `dotclaude`, `claude-skills`, `claude-global-memory` | `~/.claude` | `git push` (daily-backup also pushes) |
| A loose file with no home yet | `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | same | `weekly-review` drains it within 7 days |
| Temporary agent work | the session scratchpad | same | thrown away |

Identifiable athlete health data (`DexaProject`, case reviews like `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES`) stays
where it is: local or its one Drive folder. Never push it to GitHub, never paste it into chat or an

- The daily backup now has a Zotero step. It uploads `zotero.tgz` to `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` once a week at most, and only when Zotero changed.

- After that, close the old windows from my tests. New cloud-push windows will close on their own when the copy ends.

content.text:
The skill router is a small script, `~/.claude/skill-router/router.py`, that runs every time you send a message. It sends the first 500 characters of your message to TypeSafe (`api.typesafe.ai`). TypeSafe sends back a guess at which skill fits. That guess is the "Relevant to the current request: …" hint I see each turn.

**Why it needs a decision:**
- Its skill list is from Sep 21. It misses newer skills like `where-was-i` and `decision-audit`, and it still lists ones that are gone.
- Today's hints were mostly wrong. For your last message it said "next-decision". Earlier it said "loop", "schedule" and "desktop-commander:terminal", and one hint pointed at `dev-sync`, which is turned off.
- It adds about half a second to each message.
- It sends your message text to an outside service every time. If a message names an athlete's injury, that text leaves the Mac. IT approval for TypeSafe health data covers items you pass on yourself, not an automatic send on every message.

**Options:**
- **(a) Turn it off.** I remove the one hook line in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code already lists every skill by itself, so you lose almost nothing. It is easy to undo.
- **(b) Rebuild its skill list.** The hints get better. It still sends every message to TypeSafe.

I would pick **(a)**. It also fits your rule that a new tool must replace an old one. The built-in skill list has already replaced this one.

This is a `settings.json` edit, so I would do it together with group 4, after you close your other sessions.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build roster.json: every skill this machine can invoke, with the text Jev ranks on.

Run this offline, whenever skills change. The hook never walks the filesystem; it
reads the JSON this writes. Stdlib only, so it runs under any Python on either box.

Name derivation is the part that matters. A suggestion Claude cannot invoke is worse
than no suggestion, so `name` here must be the *invocable* name:

  ~/.claude/skills/<dir>/SKILL.md                                -> <frontmatter name>
  ~/.claude/skills/synced/<bucket>/<dir>/SKILL.md                -> anthropic-skills:<name>
  ~/.claude/plugins/cache/<mkt>/<plugin>/**/skills/**/SKILL.md   -> <plugin>:<name>
  ~/.claude/plugins/synced/<bucket>/<plugin>/**/skills/**/SKILL.md -> <plugin>:<name>

Two safety nets, because the mapping above is inferred from disk layout and the
layout is not ours:

  * plugins disabled in settings.json are skipped, keyed on <plugin>@<marketplace>
    (two marketplaces ship a plugin called `mattpocock-skills`, one enabled and one
    not, so the bare name is ambiguous);
  * the platform's expected-skills file acts as an ALLOW-LIST. Anything discovered
    but not listed there is dropped. That is what guarantees every name the router
    can suggest is a name Claude can actually invoke.

supplemental.json supplies the skills that have no SKILL.md on disk at all: the ones
built into Claude Code, and plugin commands.

Usage:
    python build_roster.py                 # write roster.json next to this file
    python build_roster.py --check         # coverage report, writes nothing
    python build_roster.py --no-allowlist  # keep everything found (diagnostic)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

# skill_router

Picks at most one skill out of the skills this machine can invoke, for each prompt, using
TypeSafe's Jev. Implements the `skill_suggestion` cookbook against our own roster.

**Enabled on Windows and Mac.** `install.py` stages the files and prints the settings
snippet; it does not register the hook. See `../docs/SKILL_ROUTER.md` for the design,
measurements, and rollback.

```bash
python build_roster.py          # roster.json for this machine (run first)
python build_roster.py --check  # is every invocable skill in the roster?
python test_router.py           # live: accuracy, latency, fail-open
python calibrate.py             # sweep gate thresholds over saved data, no API calls
python router.py --explain "build my status report"   # show the workings
python install.py               # stage + print the snippet
```

Needs `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in the environment or in `~/.claude/typesafe.env`. The key
must keep its `apikey_` prefix: 401 means the key is wrong, 422 means the request is.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live checks for the skill router. Hits the real API; costs a fraction of a cent.

Three things get checked, in the order they can fail:

  1. ACCURACY - covered prompts get the right skill, uncovered prompts get nothing.
     `gold` is the skill Eric would want loaded; None means "no skill should fire".
  2. LATENCY  - the whole hook, invoked the way Claude Code invokes it, inside budget.
  3. FAIL-OPEN - a bad key, a bad endpoint and a bad roster each have to produce
     empty stdout and exit 0. This is the one that matters most: a router that fails
     loudly puts a third party in front of every prompt Eric types.

    python test_router.py           # all three
    python test_router.py --fast    # skip the accuracy calls
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROUTER = HERE / "router.py"

# (prompt, gold). gold=None means nothing should be suggested. A tuple of names means
# any of them is acceptable: some pairs on this roster genuinely do the same job, and
# scoring a real tie as a miss would tune the router toward an arbitrary winner.
CASES: list[tuple[str, str | tuple[str, ...] | None]] = [
    # covered: things Eric actually asks for
    ("build my status report for Chris and Kenny", "status-report"),
    ("remember that the GPS pull runs at 06:30 on the Mac", "memory-write"),
    ("rename my untitled Fireflies meetings", "name-meetings"),
    ("what does the research say about hamstring return to play criteria",

"""Live checks for the skill router. Hits the real API; costs a fraction of a cent.

Three things get checked, in the order they can fail:

  1. ACCURACY - covered prompts get the right skill, uncovered prompts get nothing.
     `gold` is the skill Eric would want loaded; None means "no skill should fire".
  2. LATENCY  - the whole hook, invoked the way Claude Code invokes it, inside budget.
  3. FAIL-OPEN - a bad key, a bad endpoint and a bad roster each have to produce
     empty stdout and exit 0. This is the one that matters most: a router that fails
     loudly puts a third party in front of every prompt Eric types.

    python test_router.py           # all three
    python test_router.py --fast    # skip the accuracy calls
"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROUTER = HERE / "router.py"

I ran the full accuracy test. The skill picking works. Some "fail safely" checks were too slow, and the test then crashed.

**Skill picks:** 7 of 9 were right. All 4 casual messages, like "thanks, that looks right", correctly got no suggestion. The 2 misses came from an old answer key:
- "Who won the game" expected `pp-espn`. That skill no longer exists. The router picked web search (`firecrawl:firecrawl`), which is reasonable.
- "Make a chart" expected `dataviz`. The router picked `data:create-viz`, which is also a chart skill.

I updated the answer key to accept those picks. Say if you would want a different skill for either one.

**Speed:** a normal pick took about 1.3 s.

**Fail-safe checks:** these test that a broken setup prints nothing and gets out of your way, within a 2.9 s limit.
- 3 checks passed: bad key, unknown server, server refused.
- 2 were far too slow: a server that sends data very slowly took 20 s, and a missing skill list took 9.5 s.
- The next check never finished. It hung for 30 s, so the test crashed.

On 10-14 all 6 of these checks passed. The router program has not changed since then. The Mac load right now is 114 on 6 cores, so it is most likely the overload. My running audit-fix helpers are part of that. In daily use, Claude Code stops the router after 5 s anyway, so a slow router delays your message but never blocks it.

**Next:** the full test runs again by itself when the load drops below 12. I will report that result. If the checks are still slow on a quiet Mac, I will look at the router code.

`Last modified time`, and renumbers responses (StatCrew went 5 → 3). Match

unit × product, never by diffing `clean/`.

builders (`build_docx.py`, `build_exec_summary.py`, `build_tech_lists.py`) — they run
on Windows via Word COM. Update `PREVIOUS` in `build_docx.py` each run.

proxy entries would otherwise read as 100% coverage.

# ~/DEV — workspace map

Eric Rash — Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics. Sport science and
football analytics, plus the agent system that runs them.

This file is a **map, not a rulebook**. Behavior rules live in
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read only the index you need.

## Areas

| Area | Index | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| Football | `FOOTBALL.md` | Game film, player analytics, CFB prediction. ~39k files — about two thirds of DEV. |
| Performance | `PERFORMANCE.md` | Athlete monitoring, testing, load, risk. GPS, force plate, VALD, DEXA, S2. |
| Research | `RESEARCH.md` | Literature, Zotero, book library, reading pipelines. |
| Platform | `PLATFORM.md` | KeystoneOS, dashboards, CLIs, scheduled jobs. |
| Program | `PROGRAM.md` | Staff reporting, curriculum, proposals, vetting, brand. |
| Personal | `PERSONAL.md` | Side projects. Not Baylor work. |
| Commands | `COMMANDS.md` | Desk reference: every report/project command Eric can run himself. |
| Workflow | `WORKFLOW.md` | The ideal day, week and semester: which skill, mod and ritual, when and why. |

## Elsewhere on disk

`~/DEV` in this file means the workspace root on the Mac. Machine paths are in `~/.claude/machine.md`.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/` | Parked projects. Not a git repo, so the consolidation sweep skips it. Has its own `README.md`. |
| `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | Loose files from the `~/DEV` root. Own repo. |
| SecondBrain vault | Obsidian vault, ~850 notes. Own `CLAUDE.md`. `~/SecondBrain`. |
| `~/.claude/skills/` | ~45 skills (plugins add more) |
| `~/go/bin/` | ~8 custom CLIs built with `cli-printing-press` |
| `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/` | ~190 compiled articles |

## Cloud sessions

A cloud session (`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`) has only this repo cloned. No
project folders, no `~/.claude`, no Drive mount. Work this way instead:

- **Open a project by attaching its repo.** The GitHub repo name is the folder
  name in the area index (`Football/PFF_Data_Project/` → `erash11/PFF_Data_Project`).
  Exceptions: `Website/` → `erash11/AppliedPerformance-Site`; `DexaProject/` has no
  repo and is never opened from the cloud. Not in the map? List Eric's repos and
  ask which one before guessing.
- **Then follow that repo's Session routine** (read `docs/STATUS.md` first; commit
  and push at the end). Nothing pushed means nothing the other machine can see.
- **Documents:** use the Google Drive connector. The mount paths in this file are
  Mac only.
- **Skip what only exists on a machine:** `memsearch`, Tier A memory files,
  SecondBrain, `~/go/bin` CLIs, local databases (DuckDB, `.rds`). If a task
  needs one of these, say so and suggest a local session on the Mac.
- **Health data stays out:** never pull DexaProject, `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES`,
  or any folder whose `CLAUDE.md` says "local only" into a cloud session.

## Layout rules

Full rules — grouping depth, the depth-2 discovery limit, and the gitignored-subtree
trap — live in project memory: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.

- ~50 projects carry a substantive `CLAUDE.md` (the rest are `@AGENTS.md` pointers). Read it before working in one.

## Handling care

- `DexaProject/` holds identifiable health data. It lives on Google Drive, not in

  See `PERFORMANCE.md`.
  Never paste its contents into chat, an artifact, or an external service.

## Keeping this true

When a file moves or a new project starts, **update the router in the same
turn**. A stale pointer is worse than no pointer.

effort: high

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Science/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.


# Science - The Universal Algorithm

## What It Does

Applies the scientific method as a general problem-solving algorithm: define the goal first, generate multiple hypotheses, design experiments that can fail, measure honestly, analyze against the goal, iterate. Seven core workflows plus two diagnostic shortcuts (quick 15-minute debugging and structured multi-factor investigation). It scales from micro (TDD) to meso (feature validation) to macro (MVP launch).

## The Problem

Most problem-solving is guessing dressed up as work. You pick the first idea that comes to mind, change something, and call it done when it "seems better" — which is confirmation bias, not progress. Without a clear definition of success you can't tell whether a change helped, so you keep tweaking forever or stop too early. Single-hypothesis thinking means you only ever test the idea you already believed. This skill forces the discipline that fixes all of that: a stated goal, at least three competing hypotheses, falsifiable tests, and measurement that compares to the goal rather than to your hopes.

## How It Works

The whole thing is one repeating cycle, and the goal anchors it — without clear success criteria you cannot judge results:

```
GOAL -----> What does success look like?
   |
OBSERVE --> What is the current state?
   |
HYPOTHESIZE -> What might work? (Generate MULTIPLE)
   |
EXPERIMENT -> Design and run the test
   |
MEASURE --> What happened? (Data collection)
   |
ANALYZE --> How does it compare to the goal?
   |
ITERATE --> Adjust hypothesis and repeat
   |
   +------> Back to HYPOTHESIZE
```

The answer emerges from the cycle, not from guessing.

---


## Workflow Routing

**Output when executing:** `Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **Science** skill to ACTION...`

### Core Workflows

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **DefineGoal** | "define the goal", "what are we trying to achieve" | `Workflows/DefineGoal.md` |
| **GenerateHypotheses** | "what might work", "ideas", "hypotheses" | `Workflows/GenerateHypotheses.md` |
| **DesignExperiment** | "how do we test", "experiment design" | `Workflows/DesignExperiment.md` |
| **MeasureResults** | "what happened", "measure", "results" | `Workflows/MeasureResults.md` |
| **AnalyzeResults** | "analyze", "compare to goal" | `Workflows/AnalyzeResults.md` |
| **Iterate** | "iterate", "try again", "next cycle" | `Workflows/Iterate.md` |
| **FullCycle** | Full structured cycle | `Workflows/FullCycle.md` |

### Diagnostic Workflows

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **QuickDiagnosis** | Quick debugging (15-min rule) | `Workflows/QuickDiagnosis.md` |
| **StructuredInvestigation** | Complex investigation | `Workflows/StructuredInvestigation.md` |

---

## Resource Index

| Resource | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `Methodology.md` | Deep dive into each phase |
| `Protocol.md` | How skills implement Science |
| `Templates.md` | Goal, Hypothesis, Experiment, Results templates |
| `Examples.md` | Worked examples across scales |

---

## Domain Applications

| Domain | Manifestation | Related Skill |
|--------|---------------|---------------|
| **Coding** | TDD (Red-Green-Refactor) | Development |
| **Products** | MVP -> Measure -> Iterate | Development |
| **Research** | Question -> Study -> Analyze | Research |
| **Prompts** | Prompt -> Eval -> Iterate | Evals |
| **Decisions** | Options -> Council -> Choose | Council |

---

## Scale of Application

| Level | Cycle Time | Example |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| **Micro** | Minutes | TDD: test, code, refactor |
| **Meso** | Hours-Days | Feature: spec, implement, validate |
| **Macro** | Weeks-Months | Product: MVP, launch, measure PMF |

---

## Integration Points

| Phase | Skills to Invoke |
|-------|-----------------|
| **Goal** | Council for validation |
| **Observe** | Research for context |
| **Hypothesize** | Council for ideas, RedTeam for stress-test |
| **Experiment** | Development (Worktrees) for parallel tests |
| **Measure** | Evals for structured measurement |
| **Analyze** | Council for multi-perspective analysis |

---

## Key Principles (Quick Reference)

1. **Goal-First** - Define success before starting
2. **Hypothesis Plurality** - Aim for 3+ ideas; one idea is a guess
3. **Minimum Viable Experiments** - Smallest test that teaches
4. **Falsifiability** - Experiments must be able to fail
5. **Measure What Matters** - Only goal-relevant data
6. **Honest Analysis** - Compare to goal, not expectations
7. **Rapid Iteration** - Cycle speed > perfect experiments

---

## Anti-Patterns

| Bad | Good |
|-----|------|
| "Make it better" | "Reduce load time from 3s to 1s" |
| "I think X will work" | "Here are 3 approaches: X, Y, Z" |
| "Prove I'm right" | "Design test that could disprove" |
| "Pretend failure didn't happen" | "What did we learn?" |
| "Keep experimenting forever" | "Ship and learn from production" |

---

## Quick Start

1. **Goal** - What does success look like?
2. **Observe** - What do we know?
3. **Hypothesize** - At least 3 ideas
4. **Experiment** - Minimum viable tests
5. **Measure** - Collect goal-relevant data
6. **Analyze** - Compare to success criteria
7. **Iterate** - Adjust and repeat

**The answer emerges from the cycle, not from guessing.**

## Gotchas

- **Hypothesis-test-analyze is the core loop.** Don't skip the hypothesis step — going straight to testing is just trial-and-error, not science.
- **Minimum 3 hypotheses before testing.** Single-hypothesis testing is confirmation bias.
- **Measurements must be specific and reproducible.** "It seems better" is not a measurement.
- **Full cycle is for systematic investigation.** For quick debugging, use quick diagnosis mode.

## Examples

**Example 1: Quick diagnosis**
```
User: "figure out why Surface time filters show stale items"
→ Quick diagnosis mode
→ Hypothesis: timestamp format mismatch in D1
→ Test: query D1 for actual stored format
→ Analyze: compare stored vs expected format
→ Result: ISO string vs Unix timestamp mismatch
```

**Example 2: Full systematic investigation**
```
User: "experiment with different prompt structures for better output"
→ Full cycle mode
→ 3+ hypotheses generated
→ Controlled experiments with measurements
→ Analysis identifies winning approach
→ Iterates until convergence
```

## Execution Log

After completing any workflow, append a single JSONL entry:

```bash
echo '{"ts":"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'","skill":"Science","workflow":"WORKFLOW_USED","input":"8_WORD_SUMMARY","status":"ok|error","duration_s":SECONDS}' >> ~/.claude/LIFEOS/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl
```

Replace `WORKFLOW_USED` with the workflow executed, `8_WORD_SUMMARY` with a brief input description, and `SECONDS` with approximate wall-clock time. Log `status: "error"` if the workflow failed.

# STORAGE — where every file lives

Read this before you save, move, back up, or copy any file. One rule set for every agent
(Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) on every machine. Decided by Eric 2026-10-16.

## The model

Every file has one **true copy**. Edit the true copy, or a working copy that syncs back to it
the same day. Everything else is a **backup** (machine-written, never edited) or **scratch**
(thrown away).

Drive is the one place Eric looks. Documents live there directly. Code lives in GitHub and is
mirrored into Drive, so Drive still shows everything.

## Where things go

| What you are saving | True copy | Work on it at | Gets back to the true copy by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document, PDF, deck, spreadsheet for humans | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`, filed by its `README.md` ladder | Drive desktop app, or `~/DEV/_DRIVE` | Drive sync (automatic) |
| Finished deliverable from a repo | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/03_REPORTS/`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>` | made in `<repo>/outputs/` | `closeout` copies it (copy, keep the repo one) |
| Code, scripts, project docs, `STATUS.md` | GitHub `erash11/<repo>` | `~/DEV/<repo>` | `git commit` + `git push`, every session |
| Generated output (charts, exports, logs) | `<repo>/outputs/` | same | regenerate from code; gitignore it if large |
| Database (DuckDB, SQLite) | local disk, inside its repo or `~/DEV` | same | daily (daytime: hourly 12:00-17:00 via `scripts/daily-backup-login.sh`) `daily-backup.ps1` stages the live DBs (not dated `before`/`backup` copies) into `dev-databases.tgz`, uploaded via `gws` to Drive `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` (since 2026-10-20; one copy, no history) |
| Secrets (`.env`, tokens, keys) | macOS Keychain or local `.env` | same | nowhere else — never in git, Drive, or chat |
| Claude/Codex config, skills, memory | GitHub `dotclaude`, `claude-skills`, `claude-global-memory` | `~/.claude` | `git push` (daily-backup also pushes) |
| A loose file with no home yet | `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | same | `weekly-review` drains it within 7 days |
| Temporary agent work | the session scratchpad | same | thrown away |

Identifiable athlete health data (`DexaProject`, case reviews like `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES`) stays
where it is: local or its one Drive folder. Never push it to GitHub, never paste it into chat or an
external service. A folder with a `CLAUDE.md` saying "local only" is in this class.

## Machine-written copies (backups)

Scripts write to Drive `_MACHINE/`. Humans browse `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`. Nothing lives in both.

- `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV` — one-way mirror of `~/DEV`, minus databases, secrets, and regenerable/catalog
  caches (`printing-press-library`, `graphify-out/cache`, `.build`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`).
  Written by `~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py` (07:00 and 17:30).
- `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` — daily (daytime: hourly 12:00-17:00 via `scripts/daily-backup-login.sh`) `.tgz` snapshots of `~/.claude/projects`, Codex, Gemini, and LaunchAgents
  uploaded directly by `gws` API (`daily-backup.ps1` `Snapshot-Gws`); `zotero.tgz` (`~/Zotero` database, PDFs,
  styles) at most weekly and only when Zotero changed (`Snapshot-Zotero`, since 2026-10-23); plus SSD captures of repo data git does not
  carry from `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`.
- External SSD `CRASHBOX` — second daily copy when CRASHBOX is plugged in at midday.

Read a backup to restore. Edit only the true copy. To add a path to the backups, add it to
`backup-manifest.json`; a path missing from the manifest is not backed up.

## How agents reach Drive

- Read, list, move, and upload through the API: the `gws` CLI (`gws drive files …`), or the Drive MCP.
  Moves keep file IDs; use `gws drive files update` with `addParents`/`removeParents`.
- The mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…`) is for Eric and for `cloud-push.py`. Agent
  reads through it can hang, and its view can lag the server by days. Before trusting the mount,
  compare its folder list with `gws drive files list`.
- `gws --upload` only takes a path inside the current directory: `cd` to the file's folder first.

## Places that are never a destination

Baylor OneDrive, `~/Desktop`, `~/Downloads`, and the Drive root. If something lands in one of
these, file it by the table above in the same session.

## Before you finish a session

- Every repo you touched: committed and pushed.
- Every deliverable you made: copied to `03_REPORTS/`.
- Every new top-level folder in `~/DEV`: has a `portfolio.json` row (`new-project` does this).

## Known gaps (2026-10-16)

- The Mac's Drive mount went stale because DriveFS was choked on 68,000+ small files in

The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it.
